title: The 5 Deepest-Diving Animals, Ranked (#1 Isn't a Seal)

scenes.text: The five deepest divers on Earth, ranked. Number one is a whale most people have never heard of.

scenes.label: Leatherback · ~1,200 m
scenes.text: Number five: the leatherback turtle. About twelve hundred meters down, nearly three-quarters of a mile, on a single breath.

scenes.label: Whale shark · ~1,800 m
scenes.text: Number four: the whale shark. Nearly eighteen hundred meters, a fish as long as a bus, vanishing into the dark.

scenes.label: Sperm whale · 2,200+ m
scenes.text: Number three: the sperm whale. Over twenty-two hundred meters, hunting giant squid where no sunlight reaches.

scenes.label: Elephant seal · 2,388 m
scenes.text: Number two: the southern elephant seal. Twenty-three hundred eighty-eight meters, and it can hold its breath for up to two hours.

scenes.label: Beaked whale · 2,992 m
scenes.text: Number one: Cuvier's beaked whale. Almost three thousand meters, nearly two miles straight down, the deepest dive of any animal.

description:
The five deepest-diving animals on Earth, ranked by maximum recorded dive depth.
A whale tracked off California beat the elephant seal by more than six hundred meters.
Which deep diver surprised you most?
first_comment: Did you guess the beaked whale? Which animal record should we rank next?
